items.title: PSIRT
items.summary: PSIRT Product Security Incident Response Overview A coordinated path for product security issues Synaptics PSIRT coordinates reports of potential product security vulnerabilities with internal teams, customers, partners, and researchers, and helps manage mitigations, fixes, workarounds, and related communications. Disclosure timing may depend on customer integration, field update paths, third-party dependencies, and ecosystem coordination. Scope What PSIRT handles PSIRT is intended for security vulnerability reports involving Synaptics products and related security-sensitive product information. General technical support, commercial requests, and non-product security issues should use the appropriate Synaptics support or contact channel. In scope Potential security vulnerabilities in Synaptics products reported by researchers, customers, partners, suppliers, or internal teams. Security-impacting behavior in Synaptics product features, update mechanisms, configuration, or default settings. Out of scope for this mailbox Commercial solicitation, sales inquiries, or partnership requests. Routine product support or integration assistance. Website, enterprise IT, phishing, or corporate information security issues unless they are directly tied to Synaptics product security. Reports involving personal data submitted without consent or appropriate safeguards. Report a Vulnerability How to contact Synaptics PSIRT If you believe you have identified a potential security vulnerability in a Synaptics product, email the Synaptics Product Security Incident Response Team at PSIRT@synaptics.com . Please submit reports in English where possible. Vulnerability information can be sensitive. Do not include personal data, customer confidential information, or third-party confidential information unless you have authorization and appropriate safeguards are in place. To help Synaptics validate and coordinate the report efficiently, please include the relevant information described below under "Vulnerability Details". Vulnerability Details Product name, part number, chipset, module, software, firmware, driver, or SDK. Affected version, build number and release date. Technical description and suspected vulnerability class. Steps to reproduce, proof-of-concept details, logs, traces, or test setup. Your contact information and preferred communication method. Whether the issue has been shared with others. Placeholder for publication decision: add a Synaptics PSIRT PGP/GPG public key here if approved. If no public key is available, replace this block with approved instructions for secure exchange of sensitive materials after PSIRT acknowledgement. PGP Fingerprint: [PLACEHOLDER FOR KEY] [LINK TO KEY FILE] Vulnerability Handling Process Synaptics PSIRT workflow Synaptics PSIRT receives, validates, and assesses reported product security vulnerabilities, coordinates remediation and mitigation activities with engineering teams, and communicates security guidance, advisories, and updates with customers, partners, reporters, regulators, and the public as appropriate in accordance with established product security processes. 1 Reporting & Acknowledgement PSIRT receives the vulnerability report, acknowledges receipt where contact information is available, and opens an internal tracking record. 2 Validation & Risk Assessment Synaptics determines whether the report is in scope, assigns internal owners, evaluates reproducibility, affected products and versions, exploitability, severity, and customer impact. 3 Remediation Engineering teams define, implement, test, and validate corrective actions, workarounds, firmware or software updates, or other mitigations. 4 Disclosure & Communication PSIRT coordinates customer/partner communication, reporter updates, regulatory escalation where required, public advisories or bulletins where appropriate, and internal closure records. Coordinated Disclosure Balancing transparency, customer readiness, and end-user protection Synaptics works to coordinate vulnerability disclosure in a way that gives affected customers and ecosystem partners time to evaluate and deploy appropriate mitigations before sensitive technical details are made public. Synaptics generally strives to address vulnerabilities and other issues within the industry-standard time of 90 days after such vulnerabilities or issues are reported. Additional time may be required where many OEMs, partners, third-party components, or fielded systems are affected and a coordinated response is necessary. Policies Product security policies Current policy Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Security Bulletins Where customers can find security guidance When Synaptics issues a security advisory, the advisory typically identifies affected Synaptics products, known affected versions where available , severity information, and the appropriate path for obtaining a fix or workaround. items.title: Synaptics CRA Compliance Framework
items.summary: Synaptics CRA Compliance Framework Synaptics CRA Story What is the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)? The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is a European Union regulation that establishes mandatory cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements, including hardware, software, and connected devices. The CRA aims to ensure products are secure by design, supported throughout their lifecycle, and better protected against evolving cyber threats Learn More about CRA Synaptics CRA Compliance Framework End-to-end security lifecycle helping customers build, certify and support CRA-compliant products. Secure by Design Security engineered from concept through architecture, implementation and verification. Risk Assessment Identify, prioritize and mitigate cybersecurity risks throughout the lifecycle. Vulnerability Handling SBOM, vulnerability tracking, remediation and security testing. PSIRT Manage vulnerability disclosure and customer security communications. Secure Updates Develop, validate and deliver security updates throughout the product support lifecycle. Lifecycle & Compliance Maintain compliance through documentation, monitoring and product lifecycle support. Synaptics Secure Development Lifecycle (SDL) Security is embedded in Synaptics engineering processes to deliver secure, reliable and CRA-compliant products Security Activities Across the Lifecycle Requirement Security requirement definition Regulatory & customer requirement review Security feature planning Architecture & Design Security architectural reviews The threat modeling Attack surface and trust boundary analysis Implementation Secure coding practice Pier code reviews Static analysis (Klocwork & SonarQube) Open-source component review Verification & Validation Functional security test testing Vulnerability scanning Penetration testing Release Approval Security review and vulnerability assessment Open issue reviews S bomb generation and release sign off Maintenance & Update Vulnerability monitoring Security advisory review Patch development and secure updates Security update Lifecycle Vulnerability Identified: Any vulnerability detected from internal, customer, supplier or public sources PSIRT Assessment: Vulnerability triage, validate, and assess impact and priority following the defined PSIRT process Implementation: Develop and integrated security fixes and mitigation Verification & Validation: Validate fix and perform quality and security testing Image Signing: Sign release and create update packages Secure OTA: Deploy update securely to the devices Customer Benefits Industrial tools used in dev. process Release traceability Continuous Security Improvement Integrated process for delivering security updates Secure OTA process based on HW RoT extension Close customer engagement and collaboration Secure By Design Synaptics applies security-by-design principles embedded across architecture and development lifecycle and are aligned to industry best practices. items.title: Bagdad Hosts Corporate Interns for Annual Site Visit
items.summary: Bagdad Hosts Corporate Interns for Annual Site Visit mboyle Fri, 07/10/2026 - 13:40 Post Image July 10, 2026- The company’s corporate interns recently traded the quiet hum of the office for the din of a fully producing mine, traveling to Bagdad for a tour that connected their work with day-to-day site operations. The tour was part of the “Intern Extravaganza,” a yearly event arranged for the summer interns by Freeport’s Talent Acquisition Programs team. Nearly 40 interns participated in this year’s Bagdad tour. In total, the company has close to 200 interns this summer, a mix of office and in-the-field workers experiencing modern mining across various Freeport sites and specialties. After last year’s visit to Sierrita, the Phoenix-based interns’ tour of Bagdad has returned as an annual part of the Extravaganza. In addition to getting a firsthand look at a mining operation, the interns also learned more about Bagdad’s initiatives, including the planned Bagdad 2X expansion, the Sycamore Tailings Storage Facility beginning construction and, of course, the Bagdad autonomous haulage system. While in Bagdad, the corporate interns toured key areas of the operation, including the mine shop, SX plant, tailings, mill concentrator and concentrate leach plant. At each stage of the tour, site leaders and subject matter experts were on hand to explain the role each area plays in the site’s broader operations. The tour closed out with a visit to the mine overlook, where the interns could watch the autonomous haul trucks in action, before getting a behind-the-scenes look in the command center. “We had a really great time on site,” said Isabella Cutaia, Temporary Summer Intern-Global Supply Chain. “We saw the autonomous trucks from the upper level and control room side. I think being able to transfer everything that we’ve seen at site and what we see on our systems working from the corporate office is really helpful.” Beyond the Bagdad visit, the two-day Intern Extravaganza also included an afternoon at the company’s Phoenix Hub, where interns took part in team-building exercises, networking opportunities and heard from former interns who transitioned to full-time roles with Freeport. Alyssa Kohn, Talent Acquisition Supervisor, said the two-day event plays an important role in helping interns understand the company’s operations, connect their work to broader organizational goals and build relationships that support future career opportunities. “The extravaganza is a chance for our interns to connect and develop professionally, as well as see how different parts of the business come together,” Kohn said. “The Talent Acquisition Programs team understands how important that is and puts a great deal of effort into planning the Hub programming and site visit. It’s an opportunity to create a connected experience that helps interns see how their roles – and their goals – fit within the company.” Photo (top to bottom): Interns Isabella Cutaia (left) and Samahara Quintana Chavez take in the sights at Bagdad’s new command center; Corporate interns receive an up-close look at one of Bagdad’s autonomous haul trucks.
